blocks.x: Demand shifts by the hour across channels — we build forecasting, pricing and agentic operations that protect margin while the assortment grows.
Where the industry stands

Retail margin is decided in thousands of small decisions a day: the price on the tag, the fill rate on the shelf, the offer in the app, the allocation behind the promotion. Winners industrialize those decisions on live data — demand sensing, price elasticity, availability telemetry — and losers discover the loss later in the margin bridge, unwritten.
The pressure is structural

The operating environment keeps tightening: marketplace giants set fulfillment expectations, private label squeezes brand premium, retail media becomes a P&L line of its own, and sustainability regulation (packaging, provenance, CSRD-adjacent reporting) turns supply-chain data into a compliance asset. Store estates themselves become sensor networks — computer vision for accurate shelf data, footfall analytics, energy optimization.
How Dataq Software responds

Dataq Software builds the retail decision stack: demand and pricing intelligence on streaming data, agentic replenishment and allocation, personalization platforms with privacy architecture, store-edge vision for shelf and safety, supply-chain twins from supplier to shelf, and retail-media analytics that prove incrementality rather than correlation.
Pressure points we hear most

items: Batch demand models react to last week; promotions, weather and local events shift baskets daily. Markdown decisions and replenishment both inherit the lag.
Personalization programs stall between marketing ambition and privacy office veto; consent, preference and profiling rules are retrofitted after launch.
Replenishment and allocation by rules of thumb
Store allocation, DC replenishment and size-curve decisions run on legacy heuristics; phantom availability and overstock coexist across the network.
Out-of-stocks, planogram compliance and shrink are discovered at audit; store camera estates sit unanalyzed while OOS costs margin silently.
Vendors claim incrementality with last-touch logic; the retailer cannot arbitrate because clean-room measurement does not exist.
Black Friday peaks break cost models; nobody can state cost per order at P95, and cloud spend spikes are discovered on invoices.

blocks.x: How a delivery runs

This capability runs on the cadence set out below; the rhythm is fixed, the scope is signed. Weeks 1–2 belong to measurement: the baseline metric is captured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 run a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — steered by a control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 convert the pilot into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, and close with a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses a gate is stopped or redirected on the record.
